summary: Declare that returned evidence spends the same context budget it explains

delivery.outcome: The standard states that prompt text is read twice and that evidence returned to explain a failure spends the same declared context budget, with one machine-readable limit and a conformance check that no longer accepts a profile missing a required key.
nonGoals: No new repository: the problem is an unowned contract, not a location, and every added adoption surface is another pin that drifts.
No full JSON Schema validation in conformance; CI installs no dependencies, so only presence is enforced.

architecture.decision: Place the rule in the machine-policy layer, which the architecture already says fixes limits. maxInlineEvidenceBytes bounds what a runtime may spell out inline; anything larger travels by reference so nothing is truncated to fit. Conformance gains a dependency-free walk asserting every schema-required key is present, because the hand-written checks left new keys unenforced.
interfaceChanges: limits.maxInlineEvidenceBytes is required in a conformant profile.
Conformance rejects a profile missing any key its schema marks required.
architecture.rollback: Drop the limit, its schema entry and the required-key walk; the invariants become prose only.

validation.evidence: Measured in a Subactor deployment 2026-09-09: two comparable repairs failed in opposite ways within one hour. One carried a bare error code, kept its budget and repeated the identical failure until the retry budget was exhausted; the other carried eight rejected paths, could have acted on them, and never reached a model turn because those references exhausted context selection that would have resolved to zero files. Before this change, deleting a required limit from the profile still passed conformance.
